# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Park_2025_SNB101"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Park_2025_SNB101"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2025.1556618> (open access,
  PMC12408558); the NONMEM control stream of the final model is
  Supplementary Material 1.

SNB-101 is a polymeric nanoparticle (mean size about 110 nm) that carries
irinotecan and its active metabolite SN-38 at about a 1:1 molar ratio. Only
total (nanoparticle + dissolved) plasma concentrations were measured in the
phase I trial. The model separates each analyte into a nanoparticle (NP) form
and a dissolved (S) form by fixing the disposition of S-irinotecan to a
published model (Minichmayr 2021) and letting the data identify the rest:

* NP-irinotecan (two compartments) releases into S-irinotecan (three
  compartments, fixed) at `krel`; release is its only loss.
* NP-SN-38 shares the NP-irinotecan central and peripheral volumes and
  intercompartmental clearance, and releases into S-SN-38 (two compartments)
  at `krel_sn38`.
* 3% (molar) of S-irinotecan clearance forms S-SN-38; all S-SN-38 clearance
  forms SN-38 glucuronide (SN-38G). SN-38G leaves its central compartment by
  clearance CL3 and by a one-way transfer Q6 into a peripheral compartment
  that does not return (see "SN-38G peripheral compartment" below).
* The observed analytes are total irinotecan (`Cc`), total SN-38 (`Cc_sn38`)
  and SN-38G (`Cc_sn38g`), each with a proportional residual error. The
  form-specific concentrations `Cc_np`, `Cc_dissolved`, `Cc_sn38_np` and
  `Cc_sn38_dissolved` are model predictions only.

The model works in molar units (amounts in umol, concentrations in nmol/L), so
the irinotecan -> SN-38 -> SN-38G conversions need no weight ratio. The
NP:S composition of the drug product -- irinotecan 0.15:0.85 and SN-38
0.98:0.02 -- was put into the dosing records of the source dataset, and it is
applied the same way here: each SNB-101 dose is four records.

# Population

Twenty-one adults with advanced solid tumours refractory to, or without,
standard therapy (ECOG 0-1, no prior topoisomerase I inhibitor) received a
single intravenous dose of SNB-101 in Cycle 1 of the phase I trial
NCT04640480, in seven escalation cohorts of 1, 1, 1, 5, 7, 3 and 3 patients
(5-50 mg/m^2 as SN-38 with 8-80 mg/m^2 irinotecan; 14 men and 7 women; cohort
mean ages 58-65 years and weights 68-75 kg; Park 2025 Table 1). Plasma was
sampled at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144 and
169.5 h. No covariate was retained.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL1, S-irinotecan) | 29.7 L/h | Table 2; `$THETA(1)` |
| `lvc_np` (V1 = V6) | 54.4 L | Table 2; `$PK` `V6 = V1` |
| `lvp_np` (V2 = V7) | 287 L | Table 2; `$PK` `V7 = V2` |
| `lq_np` (Q1 = Q4) | 6.45 L/h | Table 2; `$PK` `Q4 = Q1` |
| `lkrel` (k13) | 64.4 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc`, `lvp`, `lvp2` (V3, V4, V5) | 68.6, 67.2, 127 L, fixed | Table 2 ('FIX'); Minichmayr 2021 |
| `lq`, `lq2` (Q2, Q3) | 114, 9.89 L/h, fixed | Table 2 ('FIX'); Minichmayr 2021 |
| `fm_sn38` | 0.03, fixed | Methods 2.2; `$PK` `K38 = CL1*0.03/V3` |
| `lkrel_sn38` (k68) | 0.712 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc_sn38` (V8) | 40.3 L | Table 2 |
| `lvp_sn38` (V9 = V11) | 491 L | Table 2; `$PK` `V11 = V9` |
| `lq_sn38` (Q5) | 121 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lcl_sn38` (CL2) | 167 L/h | Table 2; `FMS = 1 FIX` routes all of it to SN-38G |
| `lcl_sn38g`, `lq_sn38g`, `lvc_sn38g` (CL3, Q6, V10) | 16.9 L/h, 11.3 L/h, 7.84 L | Table 2 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc_np`, `etalvp_np` | 34.7%, 40.9%, 94.5% CV | Table 2, `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` |
| `etalvc` ... `etalq2` (fixed) | 0.0233, 0.0258, 0.0813, 0.555, 0.219 | `$OMEGA` 6-10 (Table 2: 15.4%, 16.2%, 29.1%, 86.1%, 49.5%) |
| `etalkrel_sn38`, `etalcl_sn38` | 39.6%, 44.9% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalcl_sn38g`, `etalvc_sn38g` | 115.9%, 122.1% CV | Table 2 |
| `propSd`, `propSd_sn38`, `propSd_sn38g` | 0.21, 0.416, 0.308 | Table 2 (PROP1-3) |
| ODEs | 11 compartments | Supplement `$DES` (followed where it differs from Figure 2, see below) |
| Observations | NP + S totals; nmol/L | Supplement `$ERROR` (`IND` 1-3), `S = V/1000` |
| Dose split | irinotecan 0.15:0.85, SN-38 0.98:0.02 | Methods 2.2 |

The Table 2 BSV column is `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`: the five fixed S-irinotecan
variances in `$OMEGA` reproduce the printed percentages exactly (for example
`sqrt(exp(0.0233) - 1)` = 15.4%), so the estimated ones are converted back the
same way.

# Dosing helper

Doses are given as mg/m^2 of SN-38 and of irinotecan. The helper converts them
to umol and splits each into its NP and S records. Two quantities the paper
does not print are set from Table 3 (see the next section): body surface area
1.6 m^2, a 90-minute infusion, and the irinotecan dose converted with the
molecular weight of irinotecan hydrochloride (623.1 g/mol). SN-38 is 392.4
g/mol and SN-38G 568.5 g/mol.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Park_2025_SNB101")
mw <- c(irinotecan = 623.1, sn38 = 392.4, sn38g = 568.5)
bsa_ref <- 1.6
dur_inf <- 1.5

snb101_doses <- function(dose_sn38, dose_iri, bsa = bsa_ref, dur = dur_inf) {
  iri <- dose_iri * bsa * 1000 / mw[["irinotecan"]]
  sn <- dose_sn38 * bsa * 1000 / mw[["sn38"]]
  data.frame(
    time = 0,
    amt = c(0.15 * iri, 0.85 * iri, 0.98 * sn, 0.02 * sn),
    cmt = c("central_np", "central", "central_sn38_np", "central_sn38"),
    dur = dur,
    evid = 1L,
    dvid = NA_integer_
  )
}

snb101_events <- function(dose_sn38, dose_iri, times, ...) {
  obs <- data.frame(
    time = times,
    amt = 0,
    cmt = NA_character_,
    dur = 0,
    evid = 0L,
    dvid = 1L
  )
  bind_rows(snb101_doses(dose_sn38, dose_iri, ...), obs) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}
```

# Replication of Table 3 (typical-value Cmax and AUC0-336)

Table 3 lists the typical NP and S Cmax and AUC0-336 of irinotecan and SN-38
at ten dose levels (10:16 to 100:160 mg/m^2 SN-38:irinotecan). Because the
model is linear, the AUCs pin the dose amount: S-irinotecan AUC = dose / CL1
gives 861.98 x 29.7 / 16 = 1600 ug per mg/m^2, i.e. 1.6 m^2, and NP-SN-38
AUC = 0.98 dose / (V6 k68) gives the same 1.6 m^2. The Cmax values then pin the
infusion duration: NP-irinotecan is released at 64.4 1/h, so its Cmax is
proportional to the infusion rate, and 90 minutes reproduces the printed 0.73
ng/mL at 10:16 mg/m^2 (60 minutes gives 1.09, 120 minutes 0.55). The S-SN-38
AUC, which carries the 3% molar contribution from irinotecan, matches Table 3
when irinotecan is converted with the hydrochloride molecular weight (623.1)
rather than the free base (586.7; 98.86 vs 98.68 ng*h/mL).

```{r table3-sim}
t3_doses <- data.frame(dose_sn38 = seq(10, 100, by = 10)) |>
  mutate(
    dose_iri = 1.6 * dose_sn38,
    dose_label = paste0(dose_sn38, ":", dose_iri)
  )
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 6, by = 0.01), seq(6, 336, by = 0.5))))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(t3_doses)), function(i) {
  ev <- snb101_events(t3_doses$dose_sn38[i], t3_doses$dose_iri[i], grid)
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)) |>
    mutate(dose_label = t3_doses$dose_label[i])
}))

typ_long <- typ |>
  transmute(
    dose_label, time,
    `NP-irinotecan` = Cc_np * mw[["irinotecan"]] / 1000,
    `S-irinotecan` = Cc_dissolved * mw[["irinotecan"]] / 1000,
    `NP-SN-38` = Cc_sn38_np * mw[["sn38"]] / 1000,
    `S-SN-38` = Cc_sn38_dissolved * mw[["sn38"]] / 1000
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(dose_label, time), names_to = "form", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(id = 1L, conc = pmax(conc, 0))
```

```{r table3-pknca}
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(typ_long, conc ~ time | form + dose_label / id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 336, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_typ <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, intervals = intervals))

ref_t3 <- tribble(
  ~dose_label, ~form, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "10:16", "NP-irinotecan", 0.73, 1.10, "10:16", "S-irinotecan", 168.72, 861.98,
  "10:16", "NP-SN-38", 164.95, 404.73, "10:16", "S-SN-38", 23.53, 98.68,
  "20:32", "NP-irinotecan", 1.46, 2.19, "20:32", "S-irinotecan", 337.45, 1723.97,
  "20:32", "NP-SN-38", 329.91, 809.46, "20:32", "S-SN-38", 47.06, 197.37,
  "30:48", "NP-irinotecan", 2.19, 3.29, "30:48", "S-irinotecan", 506.17, 2585.95,
  "30:48", "NP-SN-38", 494.86, 1214.20, "30:48", "S-SN-38", 70.59, 296.05,
  "40:64", "NP-irinotecan", 2.92, 4.38, "40:64", "S-irinotecan", 674.88, 3447.92,
  "40:64", "NP-SN-38", 659.82, 1618.94, "40:64", "S-SN-38", 94.12, 394.73,
  "50:80", "NP-irinotecan", 3.65, 5.48, "50:80", "S-irinotecan", 843.62, 4309.93,
  "50:80", "NP-SN-38", 824.79, 2023.68, "50:80", "S-SN-38", 117.65, 493.42,
  "60:96", "NP-irinotecan", 4.38, 6.58, "60:96", "S-irinotecan", 1012.35, 5171.90,
  "60:96", "NP-SN-38", 989.75, 2428.45, "60:96", "S-SN-38", 141.19, 592.10,
  "70:112", "NP-irinotecan", 5.11, 7.67, "70:112", "S-irinotecan", 1181.09, 6033.90,
  "70:112", "NP-SN-38", 1154.68, 2833.14, "70:112", "S-SN-38", 164.71, 690.78,
  "80:128", "NP-irinotecan", 5.84, 8.77, "80:128", "S-irinotecan", 1349.82, 6895.87,
  "80:128", "NP-SN-38", 1319.64, 3237.85, "80:128", "S-SN-38", 188.24, 789.46,
  "90:144", "NP-irinotecan", 6.56, 9.86, "90:144", "S-irinotecan", 1518.49, 7757.87,
  "90:144", "NP-SN-38", 1484.61, 3642.60, "90:144", "S-SN-38", 211.77, 888.15,
  "100:160", "NP-irinotecan", 7.29, 10.96, "100:160", "S-irinotecan", 1687.23, 8619.83,
  "100:160", "NP-SN-38", 1649.53, 4047.32, "100:160", "S-SN-38", 235.31, 986.83
)

sim_t3 <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(form, dose_label, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

show_doses <- c("10:16", "50:80", "100:160")
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_t3 |> filter(dose_label %in% show_doses),
  ref_t3 |> filter(dose_label %in% show_doses),
  by = c("form", "dose_label"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Park 2025 (three of the ten dose levels; AUC0-336 is shown as AUClast over 0-336 h).")
```

```{r table3-check}
t3_check <- sim_t3 |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  inner_join(ref_t3, by = c("form", "dose_label"), suffix = c("_sim", "_ref")) |>
  mutate(
    pct_cmax = 100 * (cmax_sim / cmax_ref - 1),
    pct_auc = 100 * (auclast_sim / auclast_ref - 1)
  )
stopifnot(nrow(t3_check) == 40L)
# Typical-value solves of a linear model at tight tolerance: the only
# differences are rounding in the printed table, the sampling grid and the
# molecular weights, so every cell agrees to within 2%. A wrong clearance,
# volume, release rate, dose split or unit moves cells by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(t3_check$pct_auc)) < 2,
  max(abs(t3_check$pct_cmax)) < 2
)
t3_check |>
  group_by(form) |>
  summarise(
    `max abs % diff Cmax` = max(abs(pct_cmax)),
    `max abs % diff AUC0-336` = max(abs(pct_auc))
  ) |>
  rename(Form = form) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Largest difference from Table 3 across all ten dose levels.")
```

## Exposure per mg/m^2 and the NP share (Results 3.2)

The paper summarises Table 3 per mg/m^2 (Cmax 0.0456, 10.5, 16.5 and 2.35
ng/mL and AUC0-336 0.0688, 53.9, 40.5 and 9.87 ng*h/mL for NP-irinotecan,
S-irinotecan, NP-SN-38 and S-SN-38), and as the NP share of each analyte: the
NP form contributes 0.127% of the irinotecan AUC and 80.4% of the SN-38 AUC.

```{r per-dose}
per_dose <- t3_check |>
  filter(dose_label == "10:16") |>
  mutate(
    per = ifelse(grepl("irinotecan", form), 16, 10),
    cmax_per = cmax_sim / per,
    auc_per = auclast_sim / per
  )
auc <- setNames(per_dose$auclast_sim, per_dose$form)
cmax <- setNames(per_dose$cmax_sim, per_dose$form)
np_share <- c(
  irinotecan = 100 * auc[["NP-irinotecan"]] / (auc[["NP-irinotecan"]] + auc[["S-irinotecan"]]),
  sn38 = 100 * auc[["NP-SN-38"]] / (auc[["NP-SN-38"]] + auc[["S-SN-38"]])
)
cmax_ratio <- c(
  irinotecan = 100 * cmax[["NP-irinotecan"]] / cmax[["S-irinotecan"]],
  sn38 = 100 * cmax[["NP-SN-38"]] / cmax[["S-SN-38"]]
)
per_dose |>
  select(form, cmax_per, auc_per) |>
  rename(Form = form, `Cmax per mg/m^2 (ng/mL)` = cmax_per, `AUC0-336 per mg/m^2 (ng*h/mL)` = auc_per) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
data.frame(
  Quantity = c("NP share of irinotecan AUC (%)", "NP share of SN-38 AUC (%)",
               "NP/S Cmax, irinotecan (%)", "NP/S Cmax, SN-38 (%)"),
  Paper = c(0.127, 80.4, 0.434, 702),
  Model = c(np_share[["irinotecan"]], np_share[["sn38"]], cmax_ratio[["irinotecan"]], cmax_ratio[["sn38"]])
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  abs(np_share[["sn38"]] - 80.4) < 0.5,
  abs(np_share[["irinotecan"]] - 0.127) < 0.005
)
```

The paper prints the SN-38 NP/S Cmax ratio as "70.2%"; its own per-mg/m^2
values give 16.5 / 2.35 = 7.02, i.e. 702%, which is the value in the table
above.

## S-SN-38 half-life

Results 3.1 calculates "the elimination half-life of S-SN-38 to SN-38G" as
2.2 h. That is the volume-of-distribution-at-steady-state form,
`log(2) * (V8 + V9) / CL2`:

```{r halflife}
t_half_sn38 <- log(2) * (40.3 + 491) / 167
t_half_sn38
stopifnot(abs(t_half_sn38 - 2.2) < 0.05)
```

# SN-38G peripheral compartment

The text and Figure 2 describe SN-38G as a two-compartment model whose
peripheral volume equals that of S-SN-38 (Table 2, "V9 (=V11)"). The
published control stream, however, writes

```
DADT(10) = K810*A(8)-(K100+K1011)*A(10)
DADT(11) = K1011*A(10) - K1110*A(11)
```

with no `+K1110*A(11)` return to compartment 10. Drug that enters
compartment 11 never comes back, so Q6 is in effect a second elimination
route and V11 has no influence on any prediction. The parameter estimates were
obtained with this code, so the model follows it. The observed data support
that choice: Figure 1F shows the median SN-38G concentrations at 48 h between
roughly 1.5 and 5 ng/mL at every dose level (read by eye), which the code as
published reproduces, while restoring the return term raises the 48 h value
about five-fold at 50:80 mg/m^2.

```{r sn38g-return}
mod_return <- mod_typ |>
  rxode2::model(
    d/dt(central_sn38g) <- k810 * central_sn38 - (k100 + k1011) * central_sn38g +
      k1110 * peripheral1_sn38g
  )
g_times <- c(2, 12, 24, 48)
sn38g_cmp <- bind_rows(lapply(c("10:16", "50:80"), function(lbl) {
  d <- as.numeric(strsplit(lbl, ":")[[1]])
  ev <- snb101_events(d[1], d[2], g_times)
  data.frame(
    dose = lbl,
    time = g_times,
    published = as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev))$Cc_sn38g,
    with_return = as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_return, ev))$Cc_sn38g
  )
})) |>
  mutate(across(c(published, with_return), ~ .x * mw[["sn38g"]] / 1000))
sn38g_cmp |>
  rename(
    `SN-38:irinotecan (mg/m^2)` = dose, `Time (h)` = time,
    `Published code (ng/mL)` = published, `With return term (ng/mL)` = with_return
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical SN-38G with and without the peripheral return term.")
g48 <- filter(sn38g_cmp, dose == "50:80", time == 48)
# Figure 1F: observed 48 h medians lie between about 1.5 and 5 ng/mL.
stopifnot(g48$published < 10, g48$with_return > 15)
```

# Nanoparticle and dissolved SN-38 by cohort (Figure 5)

Figure 5 shows the individual NP- and S-SN-38 predictions of every patient.
The typical-value profiles for the seven trial dose levels show the same
pattern: NP-SN-38 dominates throughout, and S-SN-38 peaks lower and later.

```{r fig5, fig.height = 5.5}
cohorts <- data.frame(
  cohort = 1:7,
  dose_sn38 = c(5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 45, 50),
  dose_iri = c(8, 16, 32, 48, 64, 72, 80),
  n = c(1, 1, 1, 5, 7, 3, 3)
) |>
  mutate(dose_label = factor(paste0(dose_sn38, ":", dose_iri), levels = paste0(dose_sn38, ":", dose_iri)))

typ_coh <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohorts)), function(i) {
  ev <- snb101_events(cohorts$dose_sn38[i], cohorts$dose_iri[i], seq(0, 48, by = 0.1))
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev)) |>
    mutate(dose_label = cohorts$dose_label[i])
}))

typ_coh |>
  transmute(
    dose_label, time,
    `NP-SN-38` = Cc_sn38_np * mw[["sn38"]] / 1000,
    `S-SN-38` = Cc_sn38_dissolved * mw[["sn38"]] / 1000
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`NP-SN-38`, `S-SN-38`), names_to = "form", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(conc > 0.01) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = form, linetype = form)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`NP-SN-38` = "blue", `S-SN-38` = "red")) +
  facet_wrap(~dose_label, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "SN-38 (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Typical-value analogue of Figure 5 of Park 2025 (SN-38:irinotecan mg/m^2)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Visual predictive check of the totals (Figure 4)

A virtual cohort of 100 patients per dose level is simulated with
between-subject variability on the trial sampling schedule (plus the end of
the infusion, 1.5 h), and
the median and 5th-95th percentiles of the predicted total irinotecan, total
SN-38 and SN-38G are plotted (the source's Figure 4 intervals also include
residual error, so they are somewhat wider). Figure 1 of the source gives the observed medians by dose
(for example, total SN-38 peaks above 100 ng/mL even at the lowest dose levels,
and total irinotecan and SN-38 fall below 10 ng/mL within roughly a day).

```{r vpc-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251)
n_per <- 100
sample_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 169.5)
vpc_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohorts)), function(i) {
  one <- snb101_events(cohorts$dose_sn38[i], cohorts$dose_iri[i], sample_times)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_per), function(j) {
    mutate(one, id = (i - 1L) * n_per + j)
  }))
})) |>
  select(id, everything())

vpc <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, vpc_ev)) |>
  mutate(cohort = (as.integer(as.character(id)) - 1L) %/% n_per + 1L) |>
  left_join(cohorts |> select(cohort, dose_label), by = "cohort") |>
  transmute(
    id, time, dose_label,
    Irinotecan = Cc * mw[["irinotecan"]] / 1000,
    `SN-38` = Cc_sn38 * mw[["sn38"]] / 1000,
    `SN-38G` = Cc_sn38g * mw[["sn38g"]] / 1000
  )
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.height = 7}
vpc_sum <- vpc |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Irinotecan, `SN-38`, `SN-38G`), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(dose_label, analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
vpc_sum |>
  filter(time <= 72) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ dose_label, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Total concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Analogue of Figure 4 of Park 2025: simulated median (red) and 90% prediction interval."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
```

The simulated medians reproduce the shape and magnitude of the observed
medians in Figure 1: at 50:80 mg/m^2, total irinotecan and total SN-38 both
peak in the high hundreds of ng/mL at the end of the infusion, and SN-38G
peaks a little later.

```{r vpc-check}
peak_50 <- vpc_sum |>
  filter(dose_label == "50:80") |>
  group_by(analyte) |>
  slice_max(p50, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
knitr::kable(peak_50 |> select(analyte, time, p50) |>
  rename(Analyte = analyte, `Time of peak median (h)` = time, `Peak median (ng/mL)` = p50), digits = 1)
# Figure 1 at 50:80 mg/m^2: median total irinotecan peaks at about 800 ng/mL
# and total SN-38 at about 900 ng/mL. The bounds are deliberately wide (a
# factor of two); the structural check is the Table 3 replication above.
pk_med <- setNames(peak_50$p50, peak_50$analyte)
stopifnot(
  pk_med[["Irinotecan"]] > 400, pk_med[["Irinotecan"]] < 1600,
  pk_med[["SN-38"]] > 450, pk_med[["SN-38"]] < 1800
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Infusion duration, BSA and irinotecan molecular weight.** None is stated
  in the paper. They were back-solved from Table 3 (see above): 1.6 m^2 from
  the AUCs, a 90-minute infusion from the NP-irinotecan Cmax, and the
  irinotecan hydrochloride molecular weight (623.1 g/mol) from the S-SN-38 AUC.
  The model file itself works in umol and does not depend on any of them;
  they matter only for converting mg/m^2 doses and for comparing with
  ng/mL values.
* **Additive residual error.** The supplementary control stream has a
  combined additive + proportional error for every analyte, with the additive
  term of total SN-38 fixed to 0.00001 and those of total irinotecan and SN-38G
  estimated (initial value 10 nmol/L). Table 2 reports only the three
  proportional terms, so the additive terms are omitted here and the model is
  proportional-only.
* **SN-38G peripheral compartment.** Follows the published control stream,
  in which the SN-38G peripheral compartment does not return drug to the
  central compartment (see above), rather than the reversible two-compartment
  exchange the text and Figure 2 describe. `peripheral1_sn38g` is kept as a
  state so the model has the paper's eleven compartments, but it does not
  affect any output.
* **Fixed-to-zero etas omitted.** The control stream carries etas on Q1, k13,
  V8, V9, Q5, FMS and Q6, all fixed to 0; they are left out. `FMS` (the
  fraction of S-SN-38 clearance forming SN-38G) is fixed to 1 with no
  variability, so it is written into the micro-constants rather than carried
  as a parameter.
* **NP:S dose split in the event table.** As in the source dataset, the
  0.15:0.85 (irinotecan) and 0.98:0.02 (SN-38) composition is applied in the
  dosing records; the model has no bioavailability terms for it.
* **Virtual cohort.** Every simulated patient has BSA 1.6 m^2; the paper gives
  only cohort mean weights (68-75 kg), not BSA. The VPC uses 100 patients per
  dose level, not the trial cohort sizes, so that the percentiles are stable.
* **Paper typo.** The SN-38 NP/S Cmax ratio printed as 70.2% is 702% by the
  paper's own per-mg/m^2 values.
